hints.title: Apply the whole update
hints.body: Start from f1(x)=x10. The rule says to differentiate and then multiply by x, giving f2(x)=x·10x9=10x10.
hints.recap: Multiplication by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> restores the power reduced by differentiation.
hints.pitfall: Repeated differentiation alone is not the recurrence: the extra factor <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> must be included each time.
hints.pause: Use the complete update once more to find <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: Apply the power rule to the expression actually given, then retain every other operation required by the problem.

hints.title: Prove the coefficient pattern
hints.body: Write a typical term as a constant coefficient times the fixed power of x. Apply the complete update to that term to see what happens to the coefficient and to the power.
hints.recap: An update rule can preserve the power while changing its coefficient.
hints.pitfall: Track the coefficient and the power separately through both operations.
hints.pause: Derive and check a general term using the initial value.

recall.reminder: Verify a property under the recurrence update, then use the initial state to justify applying it repeatedly.

hints.title: Sum the correct number of terms
hints.body: Once you have justified your general term, factor out the common power of x from the required sum. Identify the first coefficient, the ratio and the number of terms yourself.
hints.recap: The geometric-series formula uses the number of summands, not the final exponent.
hints.pitfall: Check the first and last indices before applying the finite-sum formula.
hints.pause: Form and simplify the finite coefficient sum.

recall.reminder: Write the first terms to identify the common ratio, and use the finite geometric sum with the exact number of terms.

solution:
The first terms are f1(x)=x10, f2(x)=10x10 and f3(x)=100x10. In general, differentiating cx10 and multiplying by x gives 10cx10. The recurrence and initial value therefore give fn(x)=10n−1x10.

Hence the required sum is x10(1+10+102+…+1019). The bracket contains twenty terms, with first term 1 and ratio 10, so it equals 1020−110−1.

The answer is (1020−19)x10: C. This identity also holds at x=0; no division by x was used.
knowledgePattern: Recognise x times differentiation as scalar multiplication on x^10
